name: test_metabolite_annotation_presence
observed: 21/879 metabolites (2.39%) have no parsed annotation at all.
biological_meaning: Missing identities include both defined small molecules (for example thiocyanate tcynt_c and allophanate allphn_c) and deliberate averaged lipid/macromolecular entities. The latter are not single molecules and should not receive fictitious exact structure IDs.
suggested_improvement: For defined chemicals, curate verified identity references and meaningful names. For mc_fattyacid_c and *_MC_* averaged pools, document compositional definitions, source measurements and units with qualified class/provenance annotations.
acceptance: Every component has a scientifically justified identity or abstraction definition; no averaging pool is mislabeled as one exact chemical.

name: test_reaction_annotation_presence
observed: 53/913 reactions (5.81%) have no parsed annotation.
biological_meaning: The missing set contains BIOMASS_Mcapsulatus, methane exchange/transport, demand/sink pseudo-reactions, custom fatty-acid lumped reactions and ordinary transport. A missing reaction database link is not itself evidence of absent enzyme or wrong stoichiometry.
suggested_improvement: Annotate bookkeeping roles using appropriate SBO terms and document biomass/lumping derivations; add exact external reaction identifiers only when chemistry genuinely matches. Keep reaction/GPR evidence distinct.
acceptance: Each reaction has a correct role and provenance; pseudo-reactions remain explicitly nonenzymatic abstractions, and chemical aliases are independently verified.

name: test_gene_product_annotation_presence
observed: 730/730 genes (100%) have empty parsed annotation dictionaries.
biological_meaning: MCA locus tags and GPR expressions exist, but there are no machine-readable gene/protein cross-references. This weakens assembly/strain traceability and transcriptome/proteome joins; it does not mean the model has no genes.
suggested_improvement: Build a versioned mapping from the published Bath genome feature table to MCA locus tags and verified RefSeq/UniProt/NCBI records, preserving ambiguous and retired mappings. Do not use unrelated-species databases to fill gaps.
acceptance: Every represented gene has a supported locus/assembly provenance record; available sequence cross-references are taxonomically and version-correct.

name: test_metabolite_annotation_overview[pubchem.compound]
observed: 879/879 metabolites lack the pubchem.compound namespace (100.00%); 0 carry that key.
biological_meaning: PubChem CID identifies a chemical structure. Missing CIDs impede structure joins but do not invalidate flux balance.
suggested_improvement: Map only defined chemical identities to verified CIDs; distinguish Compound CID from Substance SID. Averaged lipids and abstract pools may have no exact CID.
acceptance: Verified compound-level matches, with structure/protonation checks and documented not-applicable pools.

name: test_metabolite_annotation_overview[kegg.compound]

suggested_improvement: Validate C-number identity against structure, charge and stereochemistry. Preserve genuine G/D cross-references under their own namespaces instead of changing their letters.
acceptance: All retained kegg.compound values resolve as the intended C-entry; absence has a documented reason.

name: test_metabolite_annotation_overview[seed.compound]
observed: 88/879 metabolites lack the seed.compound namespace (10.01%); 791 carry that key.
biological_meaning: ModelSEED compound links support reconstruction interoperability. A missing cross-reference is not a missing metabolite.
suggested_improvement: Use the official compound table and identity evidence; do not create a cpd number from the local name. Clean whitespace on already verified IDs before seeking new matches.
acceptance: Applicable mappings resolve to the same chemical identity, with unmapped lumped entities documented.

name: test_metabolite_annotation_overview[inchikey]

suggested_improvement: Generate standard keys only from chemically reviewed structures using a pinned InChI implementation. Do not assign an exact-molecule key to average lipids or undefined polymers.

name: test_metabolite_annotation_overview[inchi]
observed: 245/879 metabolites lack the inchi namespace (27.87%); 634 carry that key.

name: test_metabolite_annotation_overview[chebi]

acceptance: Each reference has correct entity type/identity and a justified relationship; species-specific or absent records are not fabricated.

suggested_improvement: Verify the KEGG organism code and exact Bath locus entry against the genome release before adding organism-prefixed identifiers. Treat syntax assessment as not assessable until relevant annotations exist.
acceptance: Each reference resolves to the intended strain/locus, with assembly-version caveats retained. Empty applicable namespaces must be labeled unassessed; retain the raw failure separately.

name: test_gene_product_annotation_wrong_ids[ncbigi]
observed: No ncbigi annotations exist (0/730); this check fails before testing identifier syntax.
biological_meaning: This is a second report of missing namespace coverage, not evidence that malformed identifiers were found. GI is a legacy sequence identifier. NCBI moved toward accession.version identifiers; absent GI annotations are not evidence of missing sequence biology.
suggested_improvement: Prefer supported accession.version links; retain legacy GI references only when already verified. Do not prioritize adding obsolete IDs merely to improve a score. Treat syntax assessment as not assessable until relevant annotations exist.
acceptance: Modern sequence identity is traceable; the GI-specific target is explicitly treated as legacy/optional. Empty applicable namespaces must be labeled unassessed; retain the raw failure separately.

name: test_gene_product_annotation_wrong_ids[ncbigene]
observed: No ncbigene annotations exist (0/730); this check fails before testing identifier syntax.
biological_meaning: This is a second report of missing namespace coverage, not evidence that malformed identifiers were found. NCBI Gene identifiers link loci and gene records, distinct from protein accession numbers.
suggested_improvement: Resolve the Bath locus tags to current or historical Gene records where those records exist; verify taxon and assembly rather than copying numeric IDs from other organisms. Treat syntax assessment as not assessable until relevant annotations exist.
acceptance: All mapped Gene IDs identify the intended Bath loci; unavailable/deprecated entries are documented. Empty applicable namespaces must be labeled unassessed; retain the raw failure separately.

name: test_gene_product_annotation_wrong_ids[ncbiprotein]
observed: No ncbiprotein annotations exist (0/730); this check fails before testing identifier syntax.

suggested_improvement: Map each Bath gene product to an authoritative protein accession.version using the genome feature table and cross-references. Treat syntax assessment as not assessable until relevant annotations exist.
acceptance: Sequence records, organism and locus agree; multiple candidates remain explicit until resolved. Empty applicable namespaces must be labeled unassessed; retain the raw failure separately.

name: test_gene_product_annotation_wrong_ids[ccds]
observed: No ccds annotations exist (0/730); this check fails before testing identifier syntax.
biological_meaning: This is a second report of missing namespace coverage, not evidence that malformed identifiers were found. CCDS covers consensus human and mouse coding regions. A bacterial Bath gene should not have a CCDS identity annotation.
suggested_improvement: Record this namespace test as not applicable in organism-aware interpretation; retain its raw failure. Never add human/mouse identifiers to force a pass. Treat syntax assessment as not assessable until relevant annotations exist.
acceptance: No fabricated cross-species identities; exclusion is justified by authoritative database scope. Empty applicable namespaces must be labeled unassessed; retain the raw failure separately.

name: test_gene_product_annotation_wrong_ids[hprd]
observed: No hprd annotations exist (0/730); this check fails before testing identifier syntax.
biological_meaning: This is a second report of missing namespace coverage, not evidence that malformed identifiers were found. HPRD describes human proteins. Direct identity links for bacterial Bath genes would be biologically incorrect.
suggested_improvement: Treat this namespace as not applicable; preserve raw QC results and use bacterial sequence resources for real gene traceability. Treat syntax assessment as not assessable until relevant annotations exist.

name: test_gene_product_annotation_wrong_ids[asap]
observed: No asap annotations exist (0/730); this check fails before testing identifier syntax.
biological_meaning: This is a second report of missing namespace coverage, not evidence that malformed identifiers were found. ASAP is a community genome resource with a strong enterobacterial focus but broader technical scope. Bath coverage cannot be assumed or inferred from the score.
suggested_improvement: Check whether the exact Bath genome is represented before mapping any features. If not represented, document lack of database coverage and rely on verified genome/protein resources. Treat syntax assessment as not assessable until relevant annotations exist.
acceptance: Mappings are made only to actual Bath features; optional coverage gaps are retained honestly. Empty applicable namespaces must be labeled unassessed; retain the raw failure separately.

name: test_gene_protein_reaction_rule_presence
observed: 119 reactions lack a GPR; 42 have GAPFILLING in their IDs. The returned set includes ATPM, biomass, average-fatty-acid construction and numerous transport steps.
biological_meaning: A gene–protein–reaction rule connects an enzyme reaction to the Bath genome and determines which gene deletions remove its activity. Missing GPRs weaken gene-essentiality predictions and the provenance of reconstructed pathways. A bookkeeping biomass/maintenance reaction or passive diffusion can legitimately have no single enzyme gene.
suggested_improvement: Classify all 119 as enzymatic, passive/spontaneous, bookkeeping, or unsupported gapfill. Add Bath-specific genes only with sequence/function or literature evidence; record AND for required subunits and OR for alternative enzymes. Record justified exceptions separately.
acceptance: Every enzymatic addition has strain-specific evidence; complex/isoenzyme logic is reviewed and tested by deletion. Pseudo-reactions retain documented exceptions. No arbitrary genes are assigned just to reach zero missing GPRs.

name: test_transport_reaction_gpr_presence
observed: 63 of 122 classified transport reactions (51.64%) lack a GPR; this test requires less than 20%.
biological_meaning: Transport defines which substrates can reach metabolism and whether uptake consumes ATP, protons or ions. Unsupported transport assumptions can distort methane, oxygen and nitrogen yields. Absence of a GPR can be reasonable for diffusion, especially gases.
suggested_improvement: Review each transport step for compartment, direction, charge transfer, coupling stoichiometry and Bath-specific evidence. Prioritize methane, oxygen, ammonium/nitrate and ion-coupled transport used by SYMBIONT. Annotate confirmed transporters; document passive diffusion exceptions.
acceptance: Transport chemistry and evidence are consistent with the intended medium; no artificial energy cycles appear; uptake/yield comparisons are rerun. A residual missing-GPR fraction is acceptable when scientifically justified.

name: test_find_reactions_with_partially_identical_annotations
observed: 109 overlapping annotation groups involve 226 unique reactions.
biological_meaning: The same EC class or database reference can describe enzymes with multiple substrates, different cofactors, compartments or reaction variants. These are candidate curation groups, not 226 demonstrated duplicate equations.
suggested_improvement: Compare actual substrates/products, stoichiometric ratios, compartments, reversibility, cofactors and GPR logic within each group. Correct overbroad/wrong references first; merge only genuinely redundant reactions while retaining evidence and bounds.
acceptance: Each group has an explicit retain/repair/merge decision. No distinct chain lengths, redox cofactors or compartments are collapsed. Regression checks cover growth, flux ranges and affected knockout behavior.

name: test_find_duplicate_reactions
classification: Harness exception plus confirmed equation defect
observed: JUnit records TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, tuple found. Before reporting crashed, the helper found one pair: GUAt2pp and XANt2pp, 2 unique reactions.
biological_meaning: Both encoded equations are gua_p + h_p <=> gua_c + h_c, although XANt2pp is named xanthine transport. Guanine and xanthine are different purine bases. The model therefore duplicates guanine transport and does not provide the xanthine transfer implied by that reaction name.
suggested_improvement: Repair pair formatting in the audit harness. Curate XANt2pp against its source and Bath transporter specificity: a candidate intended equation is xan_p + h_p <=> xan_c + h_c, but retain or remove the reaction according to evidence. Review MCA1664 substrate range and bounds rather than changing metabolites solely on the name.
acceptance: The helper runs to completion; any accepted equation conserves elements/charge; xanthine and guanine transport behavior is tested separately. Review XPPT (currently zero-bounded) before inferring restored xanthine utilization.

name: test_find_reactions_with_identical_genes
observed: 145 gene-set groups involve 405 unique reactions.
biological_meaning: A protein can catalyze several steps or accept several substrates. Reactions sharing genes are not automatically redundant. The helper compares unordered gene sets, so it also ignores the difference between AND and OR logic.
suggested_improvement: Review each group for plausible enzyme multifunctionality, substrate breadth and GPR logic. Retain supported chain-length/cofactor variants; correct unsupported overassignment. Use equation and annotation evidence together before merging.
acceptance: Each reviewed group records its rationale; required complex subunits and isoenzymes are preserved; targeted deletion behavior agrees with curated evidence.

name: test_find_medium_metabolites
observed: JUnit records TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for /: int and list. Twenty uptake-enabled extracellular metabolites are returned; 54 extracellular metabolites exist. The intended ratio is 20/54 = 0.37037, not the stale raw metric 1.0.
biological_meaning: This check reports what the default exchange bounds permit the cell to take up. It has no mandatory biological pass criterion. An uptake upper limit is a modeling permission, not a measured concentration or uptake rate.
suggested_improvement: Correct the denominator to len(find_external_metabolites(model)) and handle an empty denominator explicitly. Independently review the default medium against the declared simulation profile, including nitrate, carbon monoxide and trace-ion availability.
acceptance: The informational check completes and lists exactly the enabled uptake exchanges. Default and SYMBIONT reference media remain distinguishable and versioned.

name: test_biomass_consistency[BIOMASS_Mcapsulatus]
classification: Genuine encoded dry-mass normalization discrepancy; mechanism not resolved by the test
observed: MEMOTE computes 0.9024111134789822 g of net retained material per nominal biomass unit, below its accepted open interval (0.999, 1.000001). The shortfall from 1 is 0.0975888865 g (9.7589%). All biomass precursors have defined formulas, so this is not a missing-annotation failure.
biological_meaning: Biomass flux is being interpreted as a dry-weight growth rate without a chemically reconciled 1 g dry-weight basis. This affects biomass yield comparisons, consortium exchange budgets and SYMBIONT mass accounting. The test does not establish that measured biomass composition is wrong or that every coefficient should be multiplied by 1.10814. Products and polymerization by-products must be subtracted: total reactant mass is 12.9475401 g and product mass is 12.0451289 g, dominated by ATP turnover rather than retained cell material.
suggested_improvement: Rebuild a documented mass ledger from the original composition table and notebook, distinguishing free monomers from polymer residues, lipid pseudo-unit scaling, nucleic-acid by-products, measured versus estimated fractions, and ash/ion definitions. First resolve the separate fatty-acid representation defect. Keep a balanced GAM hydrolysis component separate from retained material and record the NGAM basis. Reconcile experimental composition before generating a named revised biomass variant; do not apply blanket rescaling or remove water just to pass.
acceptance: For any evidence-approved variant, publish the component mass ledger and provenance, achieve the stated 1 g dry-weight basis within a justified rounding tolerance, retain correct atom/charge bookkeeping for biosynthesis, specify GAM/NGAM units and assumptions, and reassess measured yields/growth under unchanged media. Preserve the original biomass as the baseline.

name: test_fast_growth_default[BIOMASS_Mcapsulatus]
classification: MEMOTE 0.17.0 assertion direction defect; no excessive-growth failure is demonstrated
observed: The model default FBA biomass flux is 0.1780041817185448 h^-1, below the test threshold 2.81 h^-1. Nevertheless the JUnit case fails. Both the installed source and official 0.17.0 tag compute outcome = growth > 2.81 and then assert outcome, while the docstring and lower-growth message expect growth below that threshold.
biological_meaning: This failure is not evidence that iMcBath grows too quickly. The nominal flux implies a doubling time of 3.89399 h, subject to the unresolved biomass mass basis. The test threshold corresponds to approximately 14.8 minutes. Passing this assertion by increasing model growth would contradict the intended biological check.
suggested_improvement: Keep the original audit unchanged and attach a version-specific interpretation or corrected supplementary assertion. Report the intended excessive-growth predicate independently; validate any updated MEMOTE release or local test patch before treating its pass/fail as comparable. No model coefficient change follows from this failure.
acceptance: A corrected check accepts a finite, feasible default growth below the stated threshold and flags a synthetic above-threshold case. Its output is clearly distinguished from the preserved MEMOTE 0.17.0 JUnit result; the original model remains unchanged.

name: test_essential_precursors_not_in_biomass[BIOMASS_Mcapsulatus]
classification: Likely genuine omission of active pyridoxal phosphate and its dilution demand; not a simple identifier mismatch
observed: MEMOTE reports one missing universal precursor, MNXM161 (pyridoxal 5-prime-phosphate, PLP; C8H8NO6P, charge -2; BiGG pydx5p; KEGG C00018). The model instead contains pdx5p_c, pyridoxine 5-prime-phosphate (PNP; C8H10NO6P, charge -2; MNXM454; KEGG C00627), with no associated reactions and no biomass coefficient. The active PLP species cannot be identified by the MEMOTE helper.
biological_meaning: PLP is a catalytic vitamin B6 cofactor. An omitted biosynthesis/salvage requirement and biomass dilution demand can make cofactor synthesis appear dispensable and obscure nutrient dependencies. PNP differs chemically from PLP by two hydrogens; renaming it does not supply the missing active form. This finding does not prove the organism is auxotrophic, nor does it justify consuming one PLP molecule per catalytic enzyme turnover.
suggested_improvement: Review Bath genome annotations and organism-specific B6 synthesis/salvage evidence, represent correctly identified active PLP and supported conversion routes with GPR/provenance, and add only an evidence-supported biomass replacement/dilution demand. Review the disconnected PNP metabolite. Do not add an unrestricted exchange or arbitrary biomass coefficient just to satisfy the universal list.
acceptance: Correct PLP and PNP identities remain distinct; the model has a documented endogenous or supported salvage route under the declared medium, a justified growth-associated cofactor demand, and no artificial unlimited source. Recheck precursor producibility, biomass normalization and B6-pathway gene/nutrient predictions against available experiments, or label them unvalidated hypotheses.

name: test_reaction_charge_balance
classification: Mixed: ten exact encoded charge discrepancies and one floating-point false positive
observed: Raw MEMOTE flags 11 of 843 assessed reactions. Exact-decimal charge residuals are PFOR +1, CYP460ipp +2, ACCOAC_1 -1, BTNC +1, MC_Average_FattyAcid -0.001, HAORipp +2, APG3PAT_MCi +0.001, ASNTRAT +1, POR_syn -2 and G3PAT_MCi +0.001. MC_AFAA is exactly balanced; its -4.44e-16 floating residual is numerical. All metabolites have charges assigned.
biological_meaning: These flags concern the consistency of encoded chemistry rather than missing metadata. Redox-carrier electron counts and charged carrier/pseudo-lipid conventions can alter proton coupling, nutrient oxidation and predicted yields. Four affected reactions are disabled by baseline bounds [0,0] (ACCOAC_1, BTNC, HAORipp, ASNTRAT); their errors are latent until a variant enables them. The remaining exact discrepancies can affect allowed fluxes. Apart from the average-fatty-acid defect, the flagged equations are element balanced, so adding/removing H+ alone would introduce atom errors.
suggested_improvement: Audit shared carrier definitions and reaction evidence in groups: PFOR/POR_syn redox carriers; CYP460ipp/HAORipp products and cytochrome electron counts; ACCOAC_1/BTNC modified biotin; ASNTRAT aminoacyl-tRNA; and the full scaled lipid network. Specify a consistent protonation convention and distinguish true electron transfer from proton changes. Keep MC_AFAA as a numerical-only raw flag. Do not silently patch proton coefficients or broaden the tolerance until the exact ±0.001 lipid errors disappear from view.
acceptance: Each revised reaction preserves both atoms and charge under a stated chemical convention, changes to shared metabolite definitions are checked across every incident reaction, and literature supports carrier capacity/product identity. Recheck energy-generating cycles and medium-specific predictions after any accepted change. Report both the original MEMOTE result and the supplementary numerical classification.

name: test_reaction_mass_balance
classification: Mixed: one large genuine pseudo-metabolite unit defect and six exact-zero floating-point false positives
observed: Raw MEMOTE flags 7 of 843 assessed non-boundary/non-biomass reactions. Decimal recomputation shows six have exactly zero elemental residual; their floating residuals are at most 7.11e-15. MC_Average_FattyAcid instead has exact product-minus-reactant residuals C +16024.959, H +31023.945 and O +1996.002. This is not caused by absent formulas.
biological_meaning: The average-fatty-acid product retains coefficient 1 after its formula was expanded from a one-unit average to C16041H31055O1998, an integer representation 1000 times the weighted composition. The weighted inputs supply C16.041H31.055O1.998 (255.9320 g/mol on that averaging basis), whereas one product pseudo-unit weighs 255932.0166 g/mol. Downstream pseudo-lipid stoichiometry and biomass lipid coefficients are divided by 1000. This breaks elemental accounting and materially changes predicted growth/yields. A feasible S·v=0 solution or positive-mass stoichiometric consistency result does not validate the assigned chemical formulas.
suggested_improvement: Preserve the seven raw flags, but supplement them with an explicit numerical-tolerance or decimal audit so six numerical residuals do not trigger chemistry edits. For the real defect, review the original fatty-acid distribution and choose a single consistent pseudo-unit representation, propagating atom counts, charges and coefficients through every linked reaction and biomass. Separately resolve the 0.999 reactant-weight sum from rounding; do not conflate that 0.1% issue with the factor-1000 error. Treat any isolated coefficient change as a diagnostic until the whole representation passes conservation and phenotype checks.
acceptance: A reviewed variant has consistent units across synthesis, activation, phospholipid synthesis and biomass; atom and charge balances meet a declared tight tolerance (or exact finite-decimal equality); mixture proportions have source provenance; all affected bounds/units are assessed if reaction scaling changes; and yields are revalidated. The unchanged original baseline and candidate limitations remain available for comparison.

name: test_blocked_reactions
observed: 256 of 913 reactions cannot carry flux with exchange reactions opened. Of those, 66 already have bounds (0,0): 58 internal reactions and 8 sink boundaries.
biological_meaning: The model contains inactive routes because of fixed constraints, missing precursor supply, missing downstream consumption or conserved-cofactor limitations. A blocked reaction does not prove that the organism lacks its enzyme. pMMO routes, several tRNA charging reactions and selected nitrogen routes are stored with zero bounds; their intended condition-specific rationale must be checked against reconstruction records.
suggested_improvement: Classify the 66 explicitly closed reactions separately; document condition-specific choices. Trace the remaining 190 through substrate/product connectivity and cofactor balance. Reopen or gapfill only when supported by Bath physiology and the intended condition.
acceptance: Report FVA under both preserved-condition bounds and a documented structural diagnostic. Every reopened route has evidence and passes element/charge, energy-cycle and phenotype checks. Never open every internal bound to erase the count.

name: test_find_stoichiometrically_balanced_cycles
classification: Potential internal loops; altered diagnostic bounds
observed: 51 reactions can participate in internal cycles under MEMOTE’s diagnostic boundary handling.
biological_meaning: A balanced internal loop can carry flux without net exchange, obscuring flux interpretation. It is not automatically an ATP- or reductant-generating cycle. Equal reversible duplicate reactions can form a harmless mathematical loop; wrong reversibility or cofactor coupling can produce more serious defects.
suggested_improvement: Start with GUAt2pp/XANt2pp and the redox/cofactor variants in the list. Compare FVA with loopless constraints and with physiologically justified directionality. Separate cycles enabled only by the diagnostic from those possible under the SYMBIONT profile.
acceptance: Document representative cycle flux vectors, compartment/cofactor changes and feasibility under production constraints. Accepted constraints remove unsupported loops without losing known phenotypes; energy-dissipation tests remain separate.

name: test_find_orphans
observed: 74 of 879 metabolites have consuming reactions but no producing reaction under the structural direction/bound test.
biological_meaning: At steady state, consuming an internal metabolite requires a replenishing route. Orphans can block dependent pathways. They can also be remnants of incomplete or out-of-scope pathways rather than evidence of an actual cellular deficiency.
suggested_improvement: Trace each orphan to a supported biosynthetic, transport or salvage source; inspect its formula/identifier and current reaction bounds first. Repair proven missing steps or document/prune unsupported disconnected scope in a derivative model.
acceptance: Each retained metabolite has an evidence-supported supply route when its pathway should function; no arbitrary source/sink is added. Recheck blocked reactions and relevant nutrient/knockout phenotypes.

name: test_find_deadends
classification: Real product-disposal gaps plus defective assertion
observed: 81 of 879 metabolites have producing reactions but no consuming reaction. The test then compares the returned list directly with integer zero (data == 0), which would fail even for an empty list.
biological_meaning: A dead-end product cannot accumulate indefinitely in a steady-state model, so its production route may be blocked. Missing degradation, export or biomass use are possible explanations; indiscriminate drains would hide incorrect chemistry.
suggested_improvement: Correct the assertion to test list length/emptiness. Review each metabolite for documented consumption, secretion or biomass incorporation; remove unsupported scope only with a recorded decision.
acceptance: A zero-result fixture passes the corrected check and a known dead-end fixture fails. Curated disposal routes conserve chemistry and preserve observed phenotype constraints.

name: test_find_disconnected
observed: 58 of 879 metabolites participate in no reaction at all.
biological_meaning: These entries cannot influence flux directly. They may be retained reconstruction inventory, obsolete alternatives or remnants of removed pathways. Their presence inflates model and annotation counts and makes scope less clear.
suggested_improvement: For each entry, either connect it through evidence-supported reactions if needed by the intended model scope, or archive its annotation/provenance and remove it from a separately curated derivative. Prioritize confusing duplicate lipid and cofactor species.
acceptance: Removal of a truly isolated metabolite leaves feasible fluxes/objective unchanged and preserves an archive mapping. Any newly connected metabolite receives justified chemistry and tests.

name: test_find_metabolites_not_produced_with_open_bounds
observed: 329 of 879 metabolites cannot be individually produced with exchange reactions opened; this includes all 74 orphans and all 58 isolated metabolites.
biological_meaning: The network cannot sustain a drain for each of these individual species. Beyond obvious missing reactions, causes include closed internal bounds and conserved carrier pools. Inability to synthesize an isolated carrier moiety does not necessarily mean that the model cannot recycle that carrier during growth.
suggested_improvement: Separate isolated/orphan species, intentionally disabled pathways, conserved pools and remaining coupled bottlenecks. Review flux status and limiting constraints per case; prioritize biomass/cofactor and methane–nitrogen paths relevant to the intended profile.
acceptance: Producibility tests record objective value, solver status, medium and internal bounds. Supported biomass/cofactor supply is verified without creating arbitrary sources or treating an unmodeled carrier pool as a reason to fabricate a pathway.

name: test_find_metabolites_not_consumed_with_open_bounds
observed: 369 of 879 metabolites cannot be individually consumed with exchanges opened; this includes all 81 structural dead ends and all 58 isolated species.
biological_meaning: The network cannot sustain a source into each species followed by net consumption. Missing downstream reactions, fixed bounds and conserved-moiety restrictions can cause this. It is a capacity/scope diagnostic, not a measurement of intracellular accumulation.
suggested_improvement: Group by isolated species, dead ends, cofactor/carrier pools and coupled pathway constraints. Add supported recycling/export/incorporation routes or narrow documented model scope; audit topology before adding sinks.
acceptance: Each accepted change has physiological evidence and is checked for element/charge conservation, effects on growth/yield and unintended alternative nutrient use. Record solver status and the exact diagnostic medium.

name: test_metabolite_sbo_presence
observed: 858 of 879 components lack the expected SBO annotation; MEMOTE result failed.
biological_meaning: 858 of 879 SBML-loaded species have no SBO key; 21 have SBO:0000247. The underlying metadata gap is real despite the inverted assertion.
suggested_improvement: Assign an appropriate SBO entity class to each of the 858 missing species after distinguishing small molecules, macromolecules and averaged pools. Fix the inverted audit predicate separately; retain the original result and verify that stoichiometry, bounds and objectives are unchanged.
acceptance: All applicable components have correct SBO metadata. A reviewed checker expects zero missing terms. Preserve the baseline and ensure annotation-only changes leave the computational model unchanged.

name: test_reaction_sbo_presence
observed: 772 of 913 components lack the expected SBO annotation; MEMOTE result failed.
biological_meaning: 772 of 913 SBML-loaded reactions have no SBO key. Of the 141 annotated reactions, 98 use generic SBO:0000375 (process), and 43 use SBO:0000627 (exchange reaction).
suggested_improvement: Classify the 772 unannotated reactions by function, then assign the appropriate biochemical, transport, exchange, demand, sink or biomass term. Review the 98 generic process terms for more specific classification. Correct the inverted audit predicate separately and verify boundary classification after annotation changes.
acceptance: All applicable components have correct SBO metadata. A reviewed checker expects zero missing terms. Preserve the baseline and ensure annotation-only changes leave the computational model unchanged.

name: test_metabolite_specific_sbo_presence
observed: 858 of 879 components lack the expected SBO annotation; MEMOTE result failed.
biological_meaning: 858 species lack SBO:0000247; none of those 858 has another SBO. The failure message incorrectly calls these transport reactions. A blanket simple-chemical annotation needs semantic review for macromolecular/lumped species; this checker tests exact strings rather than ontology relationships.
suggested_improvement: Use SBO:0000247 (simple chemical) for applicable defined small molecules. Review proteins, tRNAs, polymers and averaged lipid pools for semantically correct ontology classes instead of labeling everything as a simple chemical. Record justified exceptions and correct the inverted predicate.
acceptance: All applicable components have correct SBO metadata. A reviewed checker expects zero missing terms. Preserve the baseline and ensure annotation-only changes leave the computational model unchanged.

name: test_exchange_specific_sbo_presence
observed: 5 of 48 components lack the expected SBO annotation; MEMOTE result failed.
biological_meaning: Exactly EX_ch4_e, EX_co_e, EX_fol_e, EX_ham_e, and EX_n2_e lack the expected exchange term. The other 43 of 48 detected exchanges have it. The failure has a real metadata basis even though the assertion is inverted.
suggested_improvement: Verify EX_ch4_e, EX_co_e, EX_fol_e, EX_ham_e and EX_n2_e are external exchange reactions, then annotate them SBO:0000627. Keep transport between compartments distinct from environment exchange; fix the inverted audit predicate and verify that intended exchange classification is retained.
acceptance: All applicable components have correct SBO metadata. A reviewed checker expects zero missing terms. Preserve the baseline and ensure annotation-only changes leave the computational model unchanged.

name: test_biomass_specific_sbo_presence
observed: 1 of 1 components lack the expected SBO annotation; MEMOTE result failed.
biological_meaning: BIOMASS_Mcapsulatus lacks SBO:0000629. This test correctly asserts zero missing terms and is a genuine annotation failure, without the inversion defect.
suggested_improvement: Annotate BIOMASS_Mcapsulatus with SBO:0000629 (biomass production) in a tracked derivative. This improves semantic discovery of the biomass objective; it does not resolve the separate dry-mass normalization or cofactor findings.
acceptance: All applicable components have correct SBO metadata. A reviewed checker expects zero missing terms. Preserve the baseline and ensure annotation-only changes leave the computational model unchanged.

name: work..venv.Lib.site-packages.memote.suite.tests.test_thermodynamics
observed: Module collection is skipped: thermodynamic tests are disabled until upgrade to a new equilibrator-api version.
biological_meaning: No thermodynamic reaction-direction feasibility result was obtained. Flux/stoichiometric consistency alone does not establish a feasible Gibbs-energy profile or account for pH, redox state and membrane potential.
suggested_improvement: Implement a separately versioned thermodynamic assessment using a compatible supported API and verified compound mappings. Specify temperature, pH, ionic strength, concentration ranges and membrane conventions appropriate to the modeled scenario; label unsupported lumped species explicitly.
acceptance: The tool runs with mapped/unmapped coverage and uncertainty reported; direction changes are supported by energy ranges and phenotype checks. Do not claim thermodynamic validation from the baseline’s pass count.

name: test_detect_energy_generating_cycles[MNXM191]
observed: MNXM191 lookup fails in cytosol c, but both redox partners are present in inner-membrane compartment im: q8h2_im / q8_im.
biological_meaning: This is an audit coverage gap caused by compartment selection, not absence of ubiquinol biology. The membrane quinone pool participates in respiratory electron transfer and is particularly relevant to methane oxidation and energy yield.
suggested_improvement: Extend the energy-cycle diagnostic to use the actual membrane quinone pool, with explicit proton-side and redox conventions. Check both oxidized/reduced mappings and the respiratory reactions. Keep these metabolites in their biologically intended compartment.
acceptance: A compartment-aware closed-uptake dissipation test runs for the existing Q8 pool, reports its assumptions and flux residuals, and either rules out a cycle under those conditions or supplies its reaction evidence. Do not move Q8 into cytosol merely to satisfy the lookup.

If absent by design, retain an explicit not-applicable reason. If evidence establishes its presence, curate the actual pathway and both partner mappings before adding a diagnostic.
